item.title: Update: ANSSI's second REACTIV report: 64 new breaches, reuse of stolen secrets the one technique; SMS 2FA and IDOR cases
item.description: ANSSI's second REACTIV report of 2026-11-12 counts 64 further breaches, five at ministries, says all exploit the weaknesses already listed and names the reuse of stolen secrets as the technique, with new cases of an SMS second factor validated by the attacker and IDOR flaws combined with infostealer credentials.
item.content:encoded:
Update13 Nov 2026 04:05 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcessourcing_notebody

ANSSI's second REACTIV report of 2026-11-12 counts 64 further breaches, five at ministries, says all exploit the weaknesses already listed and names the reuse of stolen secrets as the technique, with new cases of an SMS second factor validated by the attacker and IDOR flaws combined with infostealer credentials.

ANSSI's second REACTIV situation report, published on 2026-11-12, counts 64 new data breaches brought to its attention since the first report of 2026-09-30, five of them at ministries or bodies under their supervision, with a significant fall in breaches detected or claimed at ministry level; it says all of them exploit weaknesses already named in September and gives the reuse of stolen secrets to reach ministry applications as the technique, which lets attackers extract the data legitimately (translated from French) (ANSSI, 2026-11-12). The new cases it describes: stolen technical accounts reused against a foreign-ministry library portal after a server compromise; an IDOR flaw in the payment API of a public registration portal for the hunting-licence exam, exposing more than a thousand people; an agent's France Travail account compromised with the SMS second factor validated, with the data of more than 60,000 agents and professionals claimed on a forum; and partner-account credentials from infostealers without two-factor authentication, combined with an IDOR flaw on a URL exposing file identifiers, which let attackers extract close to 1.2 million files from the CAF's VACAF service in three days. Education nationale is now put at 25 of 30 académies, with lateral movement over the interministerial network (ANSSI, 2026-11-12). ANSSI's recommendations are renewing compromised or suspect secrets first, systematic strong authentication, strict control of privileged accounts and tighter filtering to prevent exfiltration (ANSSI, 2026-11-12).

Open finding: ANSSI's REACTIV situation reports on French state data breaches: 99 since 1 August in the first, driven by Metabase CVE-2026-72898, infostealer credentials without MFA, IDOR flaws and supplier rebound, and 64 more in the second, which names the reuse of stolen secrets as the one recurring technique →

item.title: Group-IB: DarkLunnen's FortiOS chain leaves a 'service' super_admin; Swiss FortiGates are scan targets only
item.description: Group-IB found an open directory on a Latvian server that documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen and links to no known actor: a modified public exploit for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that creates an administrator named service with super_admin privileges, among other tools. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 Swiss FortiGate scanning targets, which it says does not confirm vulnerability or exploitation, and restic commands that accessed an S3 backup repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, without naming an organisation or confirming success.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLEexploitedNATOB2

DarkLunnen: Group-IB's exposed operator directory shows mass exploitation of FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that plants a 'service' super_admin account, a 4,725-target Swiss FortiGate scan list and restic access to an S3 backup repository at a 'Swiss domain'; Group-IB does not confirm any Swiss victim

Group-IB reports that in late July 2026 it found an open directory on a Latvian server that held the operator's /root/ directory, 457 files of which 35 were recovered, and documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen; Group-IB links it to no known actor and does not establish nationality or state affiliation (Group-IB, 2026-11-11). The main campaign used a modified watchTowr proof of concept for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591, designed to create a backdoor super-admin account named service (Group-IB, 2026-11-11); the recovered results list about 600 devices in Turkey (hospitals, industry and municipalities), 16 in Ukraine, 14 in Azerbaijan and 1 in Algeria, and a stolen FortiGate configuration from a Romanian organisation carried the same account and yielded 10 cleartext VPN passwords (Group-IB, 2026-11-11).

The Swiss content is thin. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 FortiGate scanning targets for Switzerland and says such lists identify scanning targets but do not confirm vulnerability or successful exploitation; a table of additional operations also lists restic commands with AWS credentials accessing an S3 repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, with production snapshots enumerated, and the report names no organisation and says that for several operations the evidence is limited to recorded commands (Group-IB, 2026-11-11). Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-24-535 lists FortiOS 7.0.0 through 7.0.16 and FortiProxy 7.2.0 through 7.2.12 and 7.0.0 through 7.0.19 as affected, fixed in 7.0.17, 7.2.13 and 7.0.20, names FortiOS 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 6.4 as not affected and offers disabling the HTTP/HTTPS administrative interface as the workaround (Fortinet PSIRT, 2025-01-14).

Exposure
A FortiOS 7.0 device below 7.0.17, or a FortiProxy below its fixed release, whose HTTP/HTTPS administrative interface was ever reachable from the internet; a device exposed while vulnerable can carry an account that patching does not remove (Group-IB, 2026-11-11).
Detection
In FortiGate event logs, an administrator named service with the super_admin profile, any unexplained administrator or local user, and super_admin logins or account creation through the jsconsole interface, which Fortinet lists among its indicators; in VPN logs, logins with accounts whose secrets sat in an exposed configuration (Group-IB, 2026-11-11).
Defender takeaway
Hunt for the account on patched devices too, assume the configuration was read on a device that was exposed while vulnerable and rotate the VPN user passwords, administrator passwords, IPsec pre-shared keys and LDAP or RADIUS credentials it stored, review VPN logs and enforce MFA, and enable private data encryption, which is off by default (Group-IB, 2026-11-11); no source says that a Swiss organisation was compromised.

item.title: WFX Phantom: stolen GitHub tokens push a CI stealer; cloud persistence meant to survive rotation; check for probe PRs
item.description: StepSecurity and Aikido report that from 2026-11-10 an attacker uses stolen GitHub tokens, not a GitHub Actions bug, to open probe pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" and then push a stealer script into workflows, CI scripts or npm hooks where the token's permissions allow, taking Actions secrets, runner memory and cloud credentials, planting AWS and Azure persistence and deleting the workflow runs. Counts differ by lab and time (more than 63,000 probes; at least 1,835 repositories where the payload ran); how the tokens were obtained is unknown, and no Swiss victim is named.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB1

WFX Phantom: stolen GitHub tokens push a CI secret stealer into repositories from 2026-11-10, steal Actions secrets, runner memory and cloud tokens, plant AWS and Azure persistence designed to outlast rotation and delete the workflow runs; StepSecurity counts more than 63,000 probe pull requests

StepSecurity reports that from 2026-11-10 an attacker uses stolen GitHub tokens of real developer and bot accounts, as a developer would, not a bug in GitHub Actions, to push a CI secret stealer into repositories those tokens can write to (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). It first opens a pull request titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from a branch named wfx-docs that only proves write access; StepSecurity counts more than 63,000 such probes by 2026-11-12 (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12), Aikido, which tracks the campaign as wfx-loot, counts 4,837 compromised accounts and at least 1,835 repositories where the payload ran, and Endor Labs counts 8,926 infected repositories (Aikido, 2026-11-12; Endor Labs, 2026-11-12); BleepingComputer reports that the compromised accounts included those of the US General Services Administration and the French government (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12).

Where the token's permissions and the repository's setup let it run, the attacker pushes a script of about 1,500 lines through an edit to an existing workflow or CI shell script, a new workflow on a short-lived branch or a hidden script that an npm hook runs, and the script collects every Actions secret, the job token, the memory of the runner worker process and credential files for the major clouds and registries, then uses the job's OIDC token to open AWS, GCP and Azure sessions (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). It plants persistence meant to outlast rotation, a rewritten AWS role trust policy with new access keys and federated identity credentials on Azure applications, sends the archive over HTTP and from 2026-11-12 through a Telegram bot, and within about a minute pushes a revert commit and deletes the workflow run, leaving a gap in the run numbers that StepSecurity calls the most reliable sign the stealer ran (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). How the tokens were obtained is not known: some probes came through the Fly.io GitHub App, and StepSecurity has no evidence of a breach of Fly.io (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). BleepingComputer's report of Aikido's findings gives the same probe title and start date (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
Any account or bot with write access to repositories you own or build from whose token may be exposed (a personal access token, an OAuth grant, a GitHub App user token), and any build with cloud OIDC trust or long-lived secrets; bots that bypass branch protection raise the risk (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12).
Detection
In source-control data, pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes", branches named wfx-docs and commits since 2026-11-10 with the messages "ci: refresh build cache", "ci: restore", "ci: cleanup", "chore: add ci helper" or "chore: add dependency audit workflow", and in CI run history a gap in the run numbers right after one; in AWS and Azure audit logs, changes to role trust policies, newly created access keys and federated credentials named wfx-ci (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12).

Triage: a probe pull request alone shows that the account that opened it is compromised, even if nothing else happened; the payload probably ran where a commit with one of those messages is paired with a deleted run (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12).

Defender takeaway
Treat the account behind any probe or payload commit as compromised and revoke its tokens; where the payload ran, rotation is not enough because the persistence is designed to outlast it, and Endor Labs says secrets rotated after the first wave were likely stolen again in 1,838 repositories (Endor Labs, 2026-11-12).

Builds on: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets…

item.title: Update: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
item.description: Apple fixed the Brotli decoder flaw on 2026-11-09 in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1, and in HomeView Software 27.2 on 2026-11-12; Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.12, lists ISE as not impacted; Apple's pages state no exploitation, so the exploited status rests on CISA's listing.
item.content:encoded:
Update13 Nov 2026 03:56 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvesaffected_productssourcesbodyentities

Apple fixed the Brotli decoder flaw on 2026-11-09 in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1, and in HomeView Software 27.2 on 2026-11-12; Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.12, lists ISE as not impacted; Apple's pages state no exploitation, so the exploited status rests on CISA's listing.

Apple fixed CVE-2026-111497 on 2026-11-09: its security notes list a Brotli component entry, "An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation", with the impact "Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption", in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and 26.7.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), watchOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and visionOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09); HomeView Software 27.2, released on 2026-11-12, carries the same fix (Apple, 2026-11-12). The Apple pages read carry no statement about exploitation of this flaw, so exploitation still rests on CISA's listing, and the iOS 18.7.12 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and watchOS 26.6.1 (Apple, 2026-11-10) releases list no Brotli entry, which does not by itself show that those branches are unaffected. Cisco's advisory is now at version 1.12 of 2026-11-12 and lists Identity Services Engine as not impacted (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Open finding: CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens industrial and software products (Desigo CC, SIMATIC WinCC, Industrial Edge, Teamcenter and Opcenter among them), Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway and RoomOS in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while most Siemens products, the Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending →

item.description: Publica's own page of 2026-11-10 says the supplier received general extortion letters immediately after the attack, never made concrete with an amount or payment deadline, while PK Softech's page names no letter; watson.ch reports that PK Softech ignores the negotiation-chat prompt Akira left in its network, and SRF's report of a concrete demand with a threat to publish remains unconfirmed by the supplier, Publica and the federal bodies.
item.content:encoded:
Update12 Nov 2026 04:28 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Publica's own page of 2026-11-10 says the supplier received general extortion letters immediately after the attack, never made concrete with an amount or payment deadline, while PK Softech's page names no letter; watson.ch reports that PK Softech ignores the negotiation-chat prompt Akira left in its network, and SRF's report of a concrete demand with a threat to publish remains unconfirmed by the supplier, Publica and the federal bodies.

Publica's own page, in a correction headed "Stand: 10.11.2026", says that according to current knowledge the affected software supplier received general extortion letters immediately after the attack, which have not since been made concrete with an amount or a payment deadline; that the federal bodies involved know of no concrete ransom demand; that Publica received no demand itself and is in no contact with the attacker group; and that it knows of no case of persons demonstrably contacted or harmed and has no indication of publication on the darkweb (Publica, 2026-11-10). PK Softech's own page of 2026-11-10 mentions no extortion letter and does not name the attackers (PK Softech, 2026-11-10). watson.ch reports that PK Softech confirmed on enquiry that it ignores the prompt Akira left in its network to contact it through an anonymous chat and does not want to negotiate a ransom; watson's reading that the denials mean only that nobody opened the link, and that the firm and the Confederation knew early that Akira was behind the attack, is its own inference (watson.ch, 2026-11-11). SRF reported on 2026-11-10, citing several sources, that the perpetrators demanded ransom and threatened to publish or resell the data, while PK Softech and Publica told SRF that no ransom demand reached them (SRF, 2026-11-10).

Open finding: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating →

item.title: Update: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
item.description: Siemens' advisories SSA-242944 and SSA-678870 of 2026-11-10 extend the exploited Brotli flaw to 15 industrial and 28 software products, among them SIMATIC WinCC, the User Management Component, TIA Administrator, Teamcenter and the Opcenter family; only WinCC OA V3.20 and BRAUMAT and SISTAR have a fix, and the mitigations differ by product, with none listed for some.
item.content:encoded:
Update12 Nov 2026 04:21 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryaffected_productscvessourcessourcing_noteactionsbodyentities

Siemens' advisories SSA-242944 and SSA-678870 of 2026-11-10 extend the exploited Brotli flaw to 15 industrial and 28 software products, among them SIMATIC WinCC, the User Management Component, TIA Administrator, Teamcenter and the Opcenter family; only WinCC OA V3.20 and BRAUMAT and SISTAR have a fix, and the mitigations differ by product, with none listed for some.

Siemens published SSA-242944 and SSA-678870 on 2026-11-10, each still interim, extending CVE-2026-111497 to 15 industrial and 28 software products (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10; Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Fixes exist only for SIMATIC WinCC OA V3.20 below V3.20 P17.1 (update to V3.20 P17.1) and for BRAUMAT and SISTAR V8.2 Update 1 to below Update 5 (update to V8.2 Update 5); Siemens plans no fix for the SIMATIC Profiling Tool and lists none available for SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC Companion, WinCC OA V3.21, TIA Administrator, the User Management Component, COMOS Walkinside, the Project Server Web Administration Tool or, in the software advisory, any of the 28 products, among them Teamcenter V2412 to V2606, the Opcenter family, PADS and Xpedition (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10; Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). For the industrial products the mitigation is to disable Brotli compression and decompression at the application or proxy layer where it is not required, and the User Management Component and, when UMC authentication is enabled, TIA Administrator also get an IIS request-filtering rule that denies the value br in the Content-Encoding header (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). For the software products Siemens points Teamcenter, the Opcenter family and Process Preparation X to knowledge-base articles that need a Siemens login and were not readable without one, tells HyperLynx, PADS and Xpedition to disable Brotli compression and block it at the network firewall, and lists no mitigation for Innexis Architecture Native Acceleration, Insights Hub, PAVE360 Automotive and Simcenter Executable Digital Twin and Studio (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Polarion, Solid Edge, Calibre, Capital and four other software products are listed as not affected because Node.js is not present or predates Brotli (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Neither advisory says anything about exploitation; the exploited status rests on CISA's listing.

Open finding: CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens industrial and software products (Desigo CC, SIMATIC WinCC, Industrial Edge, Teamcenter and Opcenter among them), Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway and RoomOS in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while most Siemens products, the Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending →

item.title: Update: Certighost AD CS flaw: Kaspersky sees a ransomware group attempting the public exploit; patch every Enterprise CA
item.description: Kaspersky reported on 2026-11-11 that the Citrus ransomware group attempted Certighost in intrusions that began with stolen contractor VPN and RDP credentials, leaving machine accounts named GHOST plus eight random letters; it does not say an attempt succeeded and Microsoft's record still lists no confirmed exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
Update12 Nov 2026 04:17 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodycves

Kaspersky reported on 2026-11-11 that the Citrus ransomware group attempted Certighost in intrusions that began with stolen contractor VPN and RDP credentials, leaving machine accounts named GHOST plus eight random letters; it does not say an attempt succeeded and Microsoft's record still lists no confirmed exploitation.

Kaspersky's Citrus report of 2026-11-11 says the group attempted to exploit Certighost with an exploit published on GitHub, requesting a Machine-template certificate on behalf of a newly created account with the cdc attribute pointing the CA at a system it controlled, and that the group later deploys its Go ransomware domain-wide through a malicious Group Policy Object (Kaspersky, 2026-11-11). Kaspersky says that if exploitation succeeds the CA issues the certificate and the domain controller name in it lets the attackers authenticate as the domain controller account, and it never says an attempt succeeded (Kaspersky, 2026-11-11); Microsoft's record has not been revised since 2026-07-14 (Microsoft MSRC, 2026-07-14).

Open finding: CVE-2026-54121, Windows Server AD CS 'Certighost': a low-privileged domain user forges a DC certificate to DCSync, public PoC since 2026-07-24 and attempted in real intrusions by the Citrus ransomware group (CVSS 8.8) →

item.title: Unit 42: Falcon C2 runs inside the browser, fed by a script tag in government webmail such as Roundcube
item.description: Unit 42 describes Falcon, a NodeJS command-and-control framework whose JavaScript implant runs inside the victim's browser and leaves no file on the endpoint, planted by a script tag in government webmail portals and web applications, among them the Roundcube webmail of a Middle Eastern foreign ministry (39 instances in that country), and by a sideloaded Chrome extension disguised as a PDF viewer. Unit 42 saw it against government bodies in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026, names no actor, does not say how the script tags were placed and is unaware how the extensions are deployed, and assesses with high confidence that Falcon and PeckBirdy are variants of one core framework.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Falcon: Unit 42 describes a browser-resident command-and-control framework planted in government webmail and web applications, with a script tag in Roundcube at a Middle Eastern foreign ministry and a sideloaded 'PDF Viewer' extension elsewhere; it shares its core with PeckBirdy

Unit 42 describes Falcon C2, also called XG and not the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor, a NodeJS command-and-control framework whose operator-controlled JavaScript implant runs inside the victim's browser, so the endpoint holds no file for it (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). A script tag placed in a trusted site makes each visit request the implant from the Falcon server, which returns a script obfuscated per browser session, and the implant then holds a TLS WebSocket to the server while the tab is open and runs operator JavaScript through eval (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). Unit 42 identified compromised government entities in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026, among them ministries and law enforcement agencies, and names no actor (Unit 42, 2026-11-11).

In April 2026 a script tag inserted into the Roundcube webmail portal of a Middle Eastern ministry of foreign affairs let the operator intercept credentials as users signed in and monitor sessions (39 Roundcube instances in that country, none observed elsewhere; how the tag got in is not stated) (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). In May 2026 a module in a Southeast Asian police web application harvested usernames and then showed a fake Adobe Flash Player update prompt to chosen users, which served the Antino implant that uses Microsoft OneDrive for command and control (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). Against a justice-department entity in another country, a Chrome extension named PDF Viewer, sideloaded in developer mode, checked in every 3 to 4 minutes for over three weeks and exfiltrated plaintext credentials for an internal correspondence system and a screenshot of a document the victim was viewing (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). The Jewelbug campaign also used an extension named PDF Viewer (Symantec, 2026-08-13); Unit 42 lists it only as a further resource.

Unit 42 assesses with high confidence that Falcon and PeckBirdy (Trend's JScript framework used by China-aligned actors since 2023) are variants of one core framework; that is code lineage, not who operates Falcon (Unit 42, 2026-11-11; Trend Micro, 2026-01-26).

Exposure
Internal webmail, ticketing and case-management portals whose templates or headers an attacker can edit (Roundcube is the named case), and managed Chrome browsers that allow extensions to be sideloaded in developer mode; Unit 42 does not say how the script tags or the extensions reached their targets.
Detection
Unit 42's four monitoring items, telemetry class first: template and header integrity on webmail, ticketing and case-management portals for a script tag loading a resource from an unfamiliar domain, especially one returning a heavily numeric JavaScript array with a small decoder loop; extension inventory for developer-mode extensions imitating utilities such as PDF viewers with broad permissions; Baidu Analytics-style cookie or local-storage keys on internal government web applications; and OneDrive traffic to tenants outside the organisation's own with repeated small JSON writes (Unit 42, 2026-11-11).

Triage: Unit 42's basis for the cookie check is that Baidu Analytics cookies are normal on sites that use that service and anomalous on internal government web applications where it has no reason to appear (Unit 42, 2026-11-11).

Defender takeaway
Compare the templates and headers of internal webmail and case-management portals with a known-good copy and list every external script source they load, and inventory the Chrome extensions installed in developer mode on managed browsers; a browser-resident implant leaves nothing on the endpoint for file-based tools to find.

item.title: Update: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
item.description: PK Softech and the State Secretariat for Security Policy said on 2026-11-10 that no concrete ransom demand reached the supplier or the federal bodies, that the supplier never contacted the attackers, that the Confederation paid nothing and that there is still no indication of publication on the darkweb, which qualifies the press report that Akira demands ransom.
item.content:encoded:
Update11 Nov 2026 03:54 UTCrun 2026-11-11T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencebody

PK Softech and the State Secretariat for Security Policy said on 2026-11-10 that no concrete ransom demand reached the supplier or the federal bodies, that the supplier never contacted the attackers, that the Confederation paid nothing and that there is still no indication of publication on the darkweb, which qualifies the press report that Akira demands ransom.

PK Softech said on its homepage on 2026-11-10, "because of media speculation", that no concrete ransom demand has reached it and that it has at no time contacted the attackers; its investigation continues (PK Softech, 2026-11-10). A spokeswoman of the State Secretariat for Security Policy told Keystone-SDA the same day that the federal bodies handling the incident know of no concrete ransom demand addressed to them and that the Confederation paid no ransom, that, as she put it, a demand to the supplier was "not made concrete with an amount or deadline" (translated from German), and that the Secretariat still has no indication that data from the attack was published on the darkweb; Publica said it also received no demand, is not in contact with the hackers and does not know whether other organisations or individuals are being extorted, which the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating (watson.ch, 2026-11-10). This qualifies the press report that Akira demands ransom: watson.ch's headline and lead say no demand reached the supplier or the Confederation, while the spokeswoman's wording leaves a non-specific demand to the supplier open, and neither the supplier nor the federal authorities confirm a concrete demand, and the Akira attribution and the data volume remain press-sourced.

item.title: ESET: Turla's Cereal runs the victim's own Exchange server as C2 and wraps transport agents to collect mail
item.description: ESET found a previously undocumented .NET toolset, Cereal, on a Kazakh government organisation's Exchange server in November 2025 and on a Romanian government organisation's from December 2025, and attributes it to Turla with high confidence. The compromised Exchange server is the command channel, answering requests on web paths that imitate Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover and ActiveSync, and a module injected into the transport service wraps existing transport agents to collect mail, in Romania configured to select messages to or from NATO and EU addresses; ESET could not determine the initial access method.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Turla's Cereal toolset turns a compromised on-premises Exchange server into the command channel and mail collector at Kazakh and Romanian government bodies, with no attacker infrastructure and no new transport agent registered (ESET)

ESET found a previously undocumented .NET toolset, Cereal, on a Kazakh government organisation's Exchange server on 2025-11-28 and, after tuning its detections, on a Romanian government organisation's Exchange server compromised from 2025-12-23; in Romania the mail-collection module was configured to identify messages to or from NATO and EU institutional addresses (ESET Research, 2026-11-10). ESET attributes Cereal to Turla with high confidence, on the concurrent use of another component publicly linked to Turla and conceptual similarity to older Turla malware, and could not determine the initial access method, although it considers a vulnerability exploit possible because the servers are reachable from the internet (ESET Research, 2026-11-10).

The command channel is the victim's own Exchange server. CerealNeuron runs on the compromised server and passively waits for requests on web paths made to look like Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover and ActiveSync traffic; a correctly encrypted request is treated as a command and a bad one gets a normal-looking Exchange error page, and ESET found no operator-controlled server and could not identify ingress addresses (ESET Research, 2026-11-10). CerealHermit is a network-less variant that reads encrypted command files from disk, and each task runs as a small .NET assembly inside a CerealRunner (mailbox retrieval, Active Directory and WMI queries, LSA secrets extraction, file operations) (ESET Research, 2026-11-10). CerealLoader, the only component written to disk in recognisable .NET form, abuses .NET VTable fixups so native code runs before managed code and is placed where trusted processes load it: the System32 wbem directory (ncobjapi.dll, wbemcomn.dll, loaded by WMI) and the .NET native image cache (ESET Research, 2026-11-10). CerealBox, injected into EdgeTransport.exe, wraps the handlers of transport agents already loaded, so "no new agent appears anywhere in Exchange's configuration"; it keeps messages with .doc, .docx or .pdf attachments that match hard-coded sender, recipient, subject or attachment-name lists and stages them compressed and encrypted on disk for exfiltration through CerealNeuron (ESET Research, 2026-11-10).

Exposure
Any organisation that runs Microsoft Exchange on premises with a role reachable from the internet; ESET names no vulnerable version, so exposure is the deployment model.
Detection
File-integrity telemetry on the Exchange host for DLLs in the System32 wbem directory and .NET native image cache files that do not match the Microsoft originals; module telemetry for non-Microsoft assemblies loaded into EdgeTransport.exe while Get-TransportAgent lists nothing new; web-server logs for requests to the Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover and ActiveSync look-alike paths from clients with no matching mailbox flow, whose encrypted bodies return a generic error page; and Exchange Web Services mailbox retrievals made from the server's own context. With no external C2 and no known entry vector, the check is a compromise assessment of every internet-facing Exchange server.

Triage: third-party anti-spam, data-loss-prevention and archiving products also inject into the transport service, but they are vendor-signed and appear in the transport-agent configuration, which CerealBox does not; the native image cache regenerates legitimately after .NET updates, so a changed timestamp alone is weak, while a file that does not match the Microsoft binary is the signal.

Defender takeaway
Treat internet-facing Exchange servers as top-tier assets with endpoint detection and restricted egress, baseline the wbem directory and the native image cache, and run the compromise assessment now, because network-only detection will not find a channel that rides the victim's own web paths.

item.title: Check Point: a Sparrow-framework supplier fronts government watering holes with a fake Chrome certificate warning
item.description: Check Point Research groups three China-nexus intrusion sets under a malware-supply entity it calls CopperDragon, a possible supplier to actors that use the cross-platform Sparrow framework; shared tooling, Check Point cautions, does not prove one operator. The nearest to the constituency is SilentDelivery, which injects script into compromised government, shipping, IT and research websites to replace the page with a fake Chrome certificate warning that pushes a "Certificate Fix" installer carrying the SquadC backdoor, with the Czech Republic, Germany and France among the countries in Check Point's telemetry.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

CopperDragon: Check Point ties three China-nexus intrusion sets to one Sparrow-framework supplier, among them SilentDelivery watering holes on government, shipping, IT and research sites that show a fake Chrome certificate warning (Czech Republic, Germany and France in its telemetry)

Check Point Research's year-long investigation groups three intrusion sets under one malware-supply entity it calls CopperDragon, a possible "digital quartermaster" for China-nexus actors that use the cross-platform Sparrow framework (FamousSparrow and Earth Estries among them); Check Point itself cautions that the use of the same backdoor or C2 infrastructure "does not necessarily mean" the same actor ran two intrusions, so this is a hypothesis (Check Point Research, 2026-11-10).

SilentDelivery, active since early 2026 against Europe and Asia, is the set nearest the constituency. Compromised government, shipping, IT and research websites, one through cross-site scripting in an unsanitised input field, carry obfuscated JavaScript that fingerprints the visitor and replaces the page with a language-localised fake Google Chrome SSL warning urging a "Certificate Fix" utility; the MSI, served from compromised cloud storage buckets, installs the new SquadC backdoor or a SparrowDoor variant (Check Point Research, 2026-11-10). SquadC can be set to run only while a browser process is alive, persists through a Run key named WindowsUpdateAssist, and offers file operations, command execution and screenshots. A second route is a spear-phishing RAR whose LNK abuses ftp.exe, with the same C2 (Check Point Research, 2026-11-10). Positive Technologies independently documented the same fake-certificate chain, with victims in Taiwan, Germany, Indonesia and the Czech Republic (Positive Technologies, 2026-08-21).

The other two sets show what follows an intrusion. OceanGate in Asia starts from an exploited internet-facing Linux server and moves through trojanised ssh and sshd binaries that log passwords, a Linux backdoor that can load a kernel rootkit, FRP and Chisel tunnels, a hidden local administrator account and an LSA security-package credential interceptor; recent SparrowDoor builds embed the WinDivert driver to share a service port such as 443. DarkWire against Latin American telecom and government bodies uses DLL sideloading of uncommon executables, SoftEther VPN renamed to system-process names, DNS MX tunnelling and WMI lateral movement (Check Point Research, 2026-11-10). No Swiss victim is named.

Exposure
Staff of public bodies, shipping, IT and research organisations who browse peer websites, web teams whose sites accept unsanitised input, and Windows endpoints that let a standard user run an MSI from a browser download.
Detection
In endpoint telemetry, a browser followed by msiexec running an installer named like a certificate repair utility and a new Run key value with an update-themed name; in module-load telemetry, DLL sideloading by rarely abused executables, and the WinDivert driver loaded by a process that is not a VPN or firewall product; in account telemetry, a new local administrator account; on Linux, ssh and sshd binaries that differ from the package-manager copy and frpc or chisel binaries; in DNS, MX-query volume from servers that send no mail.

Triage: WinDivert is legitimate in VPN and firewall products, so the signal is a parent that is a sideloaded DLL or backdoor rather than the vendor's signed service; SoftEther is legitimate software, but not under a system-process name in a non-system path; a genuine Chrome SSL warning is never cleared by installing an MSI.

Defender takeaway
Treat a browser page that offers a "certificate fix" installer as an incident trigger and stop standard users running MSI installers from a browser download; web teams of government and research sites should check for injected third-party script and input-handling flaws, because a compromised site becomes a delivery vehicle for its peers.

Builds on: ESET: a China-aligned actor's new backdoor forges call stacks with legitimate kernel32.dll…

CERT-EU, the cybersecurity service of the EU institutions, says it has seen several threat actors use ARTEX to automate their campaigns in recent weeks and has observed AI-driven activity against its own constituency that highly likely involved ARTEX; it assesses that the framework's public availability will likely accelerate adoption, notes that the public versions are independent forks since the original author withdrew the repository in October, and maps the activity to active scanning, tool acquisition and exploitation of public-facing applications (CERT-EU, 2026-11-05). item.title: Apple spyware alerts reached German MPs and ministry staff; BSI: assume the iPhone may be compromised
item.description: Apple has sent a new round of mercenary-spyware threat notifications to users in 99 countries since 2026-10-29, and Germany's BSI says Bundestag members and other public figures are among the recipients; the digital minister said members of the federal government were also warned. BSI tells recipients to assume the device may be compromised, to update iOS at once unless a forensic analysis is intended, to consider enabling Lockdown Mode and keep it on permanently once enabled, and to consider replacing the device where the risk looks high; neither Apple nor BSI names an actor, a spyware vendor or an infection vector.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

Apple's mercenary-spyware threat notifications of late October reached Bundestag members and federal-government staff in Germany; BSI tells recipients to treat the iPhone as possibly compromised, update, keep Lockdown Mode on and consider replacing the device; no actor or vector is public

Apple has sent a new round of threat notifications to suspected mercenary-spyware targets in 99 countries, according to a notification screenshot posted by the researcher Costin Raiu, who says he verified several victims' notices (The Record, 2026-11-02). Germany's BSI says several Bundestag members and other public figures have received it since 2026-10-29, that it does not know whether the alerts mean actual compromise or only attempted attacks, and that it wrote to the members on 2026-10-30 (translated from German) (BSI, 2026-11-02). Germany's digital minister confirmed that members of the federal government were also warned (Euronews, 2026-11-02), and The Record, citing Der Spiegel, reports that staff of federal ministries, lawmakers and journalists travelling with the Chancellor in Asia were among the recipients (The Record, 2026-11-03). Apple attributes nothing to any actor or region (Apple, 2026-08-13), and neither Apple nor BSI has named a spyware vendor or an infection vector. BSI notes that mercenary spyware is generally assumed to infect devices without any action by the user, for example through a prepared message that need not be opened, and that a compromised device exposes messages including those in encrypted messengers, calls, contacts, calendar, location, camera and microphone (BSI, 2026-11-02).

BSI's guidance for a recipient: assume the device may be compromised; update the operating system at once unless a forensic analysis is intended; keep Lockdown Mode on permanently, also on a new device, noting that it hampers new attacks but does not remove an existing infection; where the risk looks high, consider replacing the device, resetting every account used on it and changing the phone number; then set a new device passcode, change the Apple Account and mail passwords, re-enrol authenticator apps instead of transferring them, enable Signal's registration lock and WhatsApp's two-step verification with new PINs, remove linked devices nobody recognises, and report the notification to BSI's service centre (BSI, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
Apple sends these notifications to individuals it judges to have been individually targeted, "likely because of who they are or what they do", and names politicians and diplomats among the usual targets (Apple, 2026-08-13); a recipient confirms authenticity on the lock screen, in Settings, in the e-mail to the Apple Account address and in the banner at account.apple.com after signing in (Apple, 2026-08-13).
Detection
Apple relies solely on its own threat intelligence and says it cannot say what causes a notification (Apple, 2026-08-13), and BSI's guidance names no artefact to check, so the organisational signal is a recipient reporting the notification; unusual device behaviour such as frequent crashes or fast battery drain is the only on-device hint BSI mentions (BSI, 2026-11-02).

Triage: a genuine notification never asks to click a link, open a file, install an app or profile, or give a password or verification code; a message that does is a phishing imitation, and the recipient should open account.apple.com directly in the browser instead (Apple, 2026-08-13).

Defender takeaway
Give people who are plausible targets the authenticity check above and a named internal reporting path, and keep a replace-device-and-reset-accounts procedure that follows BSI's order; a recipient updates iOS at once unless a forensic analysis is intended, considers Lockdown Mode and keeps it on permanently once enabled, and considers replacing the device where the risk is rated high, treating it as possibly compromised until then.

item.description: The Technical University of Munich said on 2026-11-06 that unknown attackers attacked its myTUM portal and captured the central-login passwords of all persons who had signed in there, among them the credentials of a TUMonline system administrator, with which they attacked the campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM took off the network. TUM says accounts with multi-factor authentication were protected, reported the incident to the Bavarian data-protection commissioner and filed a criminal complaint; heise reports that the entry point was a legacy system and that about 60,000 users are concerned.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Technical University of Munich: attackers captured the central-login passwords of everyone who signed in to the legacy myTUM portal, took a TUMonline system administrator's credentials and attacked the campus-management system; accounts with MFA were protected

The Technical University of Munich says unknown persons attacked its myTUM portal and captured the passwords for the central login to TUM systems, among them login.tum.de and TUMonline, from all persons who had logged in to myTUM; among them were the access credentials of a system administrator for TUMonline, with which the attackers attacked the central campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM then took off the network (translated from German) (TUM, 2026-11-06). TUM says the attackers may have reached the account password, name, private address and date of birth of everyone affected, plus staff and student details, that the attackers' accesses within TUMonline were largely logged and that it currently assumes no further TUMonline data such as grades is affected, and that accounts with multi-factor authentication were protected in this attack (translated from German) (TUM, 2026-11-06). heise, quoting a TUM spokesperson, reports that the attackers entered through a legacy system and that whether data was exfiltrated is still being investigated, and adds that about 60,000 students and employees are concerned (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-11-06). Neither source states how the passwords were captured at myTUM.

Exposure
A public university or other public body that keeps a retired or secondary sign-in portal validating against its central directory, so that every password typed there is a credential for the primary identity and administration systems; TUM's accounts with MFA held, and the lesson transfers to Swiss cantonal and university portals.
Defender takeaway
Inventory legacy and secondary portals that accept the central directory password and retire them or put them behind MFA, require MFA on administrator accounts of campus and school-management systems, and check whether an administrator ever signed in to such a portal.

item.title: Aargau's information-security law and ordinance take effect 1 January 2027; a specialist unit is to get directive powers
item.description: The Aargau government council announced on 2026-11-06 that it adopted the information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and that the information-security law (InfoSiG) and the ordinance enter into force on 1 January 2027. An information-security specialist unit is to advise cantonal bodies with directive and enforcement powers, and a cantonal cyber coordination office, headed from that date by Bernhard Droz, and a personnel-security-vetting unit sit at the cantonal police.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Canton Aargau adopts its information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and sets 1 January 2027 for the information-security law and ordinance, with a specialist unit to receive directive and enforcement powers and a cyber coordination office at the cantonal police

The Aargau government council adopted the information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and decided that the information-security legislation, the law (InfoSiG) and the ordinance, enters into force on 1 January 2027 (translated from German) (Kanton Aargau, 2026-11-06). The canton says the law anchors uniform standards and a holistic information-security system in the cantonal administration, that an information-security specialist unit is to advise the cantonal bodies and be equipped with directive and enforcement powers so that one detection and defence strategy can be implemented, and that a further specialist unit for personnel security vetting and a cantonal cyber coordination office are being set up, both at the cantonal police (translated from German) (Kanton Aargau, 2026-11-06). The government elected Bernhard Droz, currently head of IT forensics and cybercrime at the cantonal police, as head of the cyber coordination office from 1 January 2027 (translated from German) (Kanton Aargau, 2026-11-06).

The communiqué says nothing about communes or other bearers of public tasks. In February 2025 Netzwoche reported that a majority in the consultation approved bringing them into the law's scope and that entry into force was then planned for 1 July 2026, so the final text decides whether communal bodies are bound (Netzwoche, 2025-02-24).

Exposure
Aargau cantonal bodies from 1 January 2027; whether communes and other bearers of public tasks fall in scope is not stated in the communiqué.
Defender takeaway
From 1 January 2027 Aargau cantonal bodies answer to one information-security specialist unit that is to be equipped to issue binding directives, so the 2026 task is reading the ordinance and the directives the specialist unit issues; the canton describes the unit's planned powers and not detailed duties, and communal IT owners should read the final text to see whether they are covered.

item.title: BOSSAI AI agents took emergency-services data through open ports, public APIs and default credentials
item.description: Acronis TRU describes BOSSAI, an agentic campaign it attributes with high confidence to one operator in Taiwan: a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, that over 12 observed days targeted government emergency services, banks, universities and military systems in 11 countries, with confirmed data exfiltration or system access at roughly ten targets in three countries. The confirmed emergency-services harm was patient-care records of a Taipei fire department and dispatch case records of a city 119 system; TRU says the agents failed where authentication was enforced and endpoints were filtered.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB3

Acronis TRU on BOSSAI: one operator's mesh of 12 AI agents took patient-care records and dispatch case data from Taiwanese emergency services through a legacy open port, a public API and default root credentials, and failed wherever authentication was enforced

Acronis TRU found an open attack workstation holding more than 90,000 files and describes BOSSAI as a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, driven by a changing roster of language models, with the operator acting as the bridge between agents and typing commands in Traditional Chinese (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). The agents that executed attacks ran almost exclusively on abliterated open-weight models run locally, after commercial models repeatedly refused offensive requests (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). In the 12 days TRU observed, the operator targeted government emergency services, banks and lenders, universities and military systems in 11 countries, with confirmed exfiltration or system access at roughly ten targets in three countries and about fifteen more attacked without confirmed compromise (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04).

The confirmed emergency-services harm is the part that matters here. A Taipei fire-department patient-care records platform exposed ECG readings, ambulance video and vital signs from 2018, accessible without credentials; a city's 119 dispatch system yielded case records with incident times, response types, status fields and street-level locations across seven districts from the system's API; and a fire-dispatch vendor's database administration panel opened with default root credentials, exposing 18 or more tables (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). In an emergency-management system the agents found a hardcoded AES-256 key in front-end JavaScript that exposed session-cookie contents, an administrator identity among them, and a partial server-side request forgery path, without confirming a full compromise (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). A brute-force run against a national fire agency's single sign-on portal gave no confirmed access, and the critical Apache flaw that the operator's vulnerability platform reported at a disaster-response centre was fabricated, because the port was filtered (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). TRU says the agents failed where authentication was enforced, where paywalls required valid sessions and where endpoints were properly filtered, and that obscurity no longer protects a system from agents that investigate hundreds of targets at once (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04).

Exposure
Emergency-service, dispatch and public-safety systems that expose a record API or a legacy data port without authentication, leave default administrator credentials on a vendor's database panel, or ship secrets in front-end JavaScript; those are the weaknesses the agents turned into data, and TRU reports the patient-care and dispatch records as the gravest confirmed harm.
Detection
TRU names sqlmap, nmap and nikto among the most-used tools, so the traffic is ordinary scanner traffic in web access and authentication logs (an inference from the tool list): bursts of SQL-injection probing, repeated sign-in attempts against a single sign-on portal from one source, and logins to a database administration panel with a default account.
Defender takeaway
Swiss dispatch, patient-care and records systems of emergency services are the same target class, so check them for unauthenticated APIs and legacy ports, default root or administrator credentials on vendor panels, and keys or tokens in front-end code; the agents failed wherever authentication was enforced, so closing those gaps is what stops this tooling.

item.title: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
item.description: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-10 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates), Gridscale X DSA V5.3 and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V5.4 and V36.8.0), Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix, and, in two interim advisories of 2026-11-10, 15 industrial products including SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, the User Management Component and TIA Administrator and 28 software products including Teamcenter and the Opcenter family, nearly all with no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2) and RoomOS among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited. Apple fixed the flaw on 2026-11-09 in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1, and in HomeView Software 27.2 on 2026-11-12.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-111497exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens industrial and software products (Desigo CC, SIMATIC WinCC, Industrial Edge, Teamcenter and Opcenter among them), Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway and RoomOS in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while most Siemens products, the Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending

The Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write caused by improper handling of malformed compressed data (Mitel, 2026-10-28), and CISA lists it as exploited (CISA, 2026-10-27). Siemens' advisory SSA-045512, revised on 2026-11-06, lists Desigo CC V8 and V9, all versions, remedied by installing the latest .NET security updates via Windows Update, Gridscale X DSA from V5.3 below V5.4 (fixed in V5.4) and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V36.8.0), and scores the flaw CVSS 3.1 9.8 (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Its Industrial Edge advisory SSA-443410 gives fixed versions for six configurator and monitoring applications, and for Common Configurator, which has no fix, says to uninstall all Management Applications and use a firewall or WAF, or stop the application on a device (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Two further Siemens advisories of 2026-11-10, both interim, list 15 industrial and 28 software products, with a fix only for WinCC OA V3.20 and BRAUMAT and SISTAR and mitigations that differ by product, some products having none; neither says anything about exploitation (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10) (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10).

Mitel's MISA-2026-0010, revision 5.0 of 2026-11-04, rates the flaw high (CVSS 3.1 8.1) and lists MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products, up to the versions in its table, as affected; for each an update is planned, not released, and workaround articles exist for OpenScape SBC, SESAP and Contact Center (Mitel, 2026-10-28).

Cisco's advisory, version 1.12 of 2026-11-12, says its PSIRT is aware that proof-of-concept exploit code is available and is not aware of any malicious use against any Cisco product; it lists Catalyst SD-WAN, Identity Services Engine, IOS XE, IOS XR and Secure Firewall ASA, FMC and FTD as not impacted (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Its single fix table lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2), Spaces (24.22.1), RoomOS on Board, Desk and Room Series devices (on-premises 11.41.2.3 and 26.7.4.3) and a longer list whose fixes are dated November 2026 to March 2027 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Siemens WinCC, UMC, TIA Administrator, Teamcenter or Opcenter system the 2026-11-10 advisories list, a Desigo CC host, a Gridscale X DSA or PSS®E installation below its fixed version, an Industrial Edge Management instance with Management Applications installed or a Common Configurator on an Edge device, a Mitel MiVoice Business or OpenScape system at the listed versions, a Cisco Duo Network Gateway or RoomOS device that Cisco lists in its combined advisory, below the builds above, or an iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch or Vision Pro below the 2026-11-09 releases.
Defender takeaway
Install the 2026-11-09 Apple releases on managed iPhones and iPads (Apple, 2026-11-09), Macs (Apple, 2026-11-09), Apple Watches (Apple, 2026-11-09) and Vision Pro (Apple, 2026-11-09) and the current .NET updates on every Desigo CC host and move Gridscale X DSA to V5.4 and PSS®E to V36.8.0. On Industrial Edge, update the monitoring and configurator applications to the fixed versions and, where Common Configurator runs, uninstall all Management Applications or stop it on Edge devices until Siemens ships a fix. Apply Mitel's workaround articles for OpenScape SBC, SESAP and Contact Center until updates ship, and update Duo Network Gateway to the 3.4.2 that Cisco's table lists. For the SSA-242944 products with no fix, disable Brotli at the application or proxy layer and apply the UMC request-filter rule; for Teamcenter, the Opcenter family and Process Preparation X use the knowledge-base mitigations SSA-678870 links.
Correction08 Nov 2026 13:54 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodycvessummary

Siemens' revision of advisory SSA-045512 on 2026-11-06 also added two grid products: Gridscale X DSA from V5.3 up to but excluding V5.4, fixed in V5.4 or later, and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0, fixed in V36.8.0 or later (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Siemens describes Gridscale X DSA as real-time grid stability assessment and PSS®E as transmission planning and analysis software (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30).

Update12 Nov 2026 04:21 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryaffected_productscvessourcessourcing_noteactionsbodyentities

Siemens published SSA-242944 and SSA-678870 on 2026-11-10, each still interim, extending CVE-2026-111497 to 15 industrial and 28 software products (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10; Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Fixes exist only for SIMATIC WinCC OA V3.20 below V3.20 P17.1 (update to V3.20 P17.1) and for BRAUMAT and SISTAR V8.2 Update 1 to below Update 5 (update to V8.2 Update 5); Siemens plans no fix for the SIMATIC Profiling Tool and lists none available for SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC Companion, WinCC OA V3.21, TIA Administrator, the User Management Component, COMOS Walkinside, the Project Server Web Administration Tool or, in the software advisory, any of the 28 products, among them Teamcenter V2412 to V2606, the Opcenter family, PADS and Xpedition (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10; Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). For the industrial products the mitigation is to disable Brotli compression and decompression at the application or proxy layer where it is not required, and the User Management Component and, when UMC authentication is enabled, TIA Administrator also get an IIS request-filtering rule that denies the value br in the Content-Encoding header (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). For the software products Siemens points Teamcenter, the Opcenter family and Process Preparation X to knowledge-base articles that need a Siemens login and were not readable without one, tells HyperLynx, PADS and Xpedition to disable Brotli compression and block it at the network firewall, and lists no mitigation for Innexis Architecture Native Acceleration, Insights Hub, PAVE360 Automotive and Simcenter Executable Digital Twin and Studio (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Polarion, Solid Edge, Calibre, Capital and four other software products are listed as not affected because Node.js is not present or predates Brotli (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Neither advisory says anything about exploitation; the exploited status rests on CISA's listing.

Update13 Nov 2026 03:56 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvesaffected_productssourcesbodyentities

Apple fixed CVE-2026-111497 on 2026-11-09: its security notes list a Brotli component entry, "An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation", with the impact "Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption", in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and 26.7.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), watchOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and visionOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09); HomeView Software 27.2, released on 2026-11-12, carries the same fix (Apple, 2026-11-12). The Apple pages read carry no statement about exploitation of this flaw, so exploitation still rests on CISA's listing, and the iOS 18.7.12 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and watchOS 26.6.1 (Apple, 2026-11-10) releases list no Brotli entry, which does not by itself show that those branches are unaffected. Cisco's advisory is now at version 1.12 of 2026-11-12 and lists Identity Services Engine as not impacted (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

item.title: Update: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs ARTEX at machine speed; Mandiant now sees agent frameworks in incident-response cases
item.description: Microsoft reports that Storm-3358, a Cambodia-based, financially motivated cluster, has used ARTEX since October 2026 against financial organisations, pairing it with conventional scanners and installing the open-source remote access tools WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2; Check Point Research reads ten exposed operator consoles showing campaigns that run almost autonomously once a goal is set, and Microsoft says honeypots, decoys, tarpits and fake wins helped reduce the attack traffic reaching real assets.
item.content:encoded:
Update07 Nov 2026 03:50 UTCrun 2026-11-07T0256Z-intelsummaryentitiestechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_note

Microsoft reports that Storm-3358, a Cambodia-based, financially motivated cluster, has used ARTEX since October 2026 against financial organisations, pairing it with conventional scanners and installing the open-source remote access tools WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2; Check Point Research reads ten exposed operator consoles showing campaigns that run almost autonomously once a goal is set, and Microsoft says honeypots, decoys, tarpits and fake wins helped reduce the attack traffic reaching real assets.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that Storm-3358, a Cambodia-based intrusion cluster that primarily targets financial organisations in Southeast Asia and a smaller number of large financial organisations globally, began using ARTEX against the financial sector in October 2026 (Microsoft, 2026-11-06). Microsoft says the cluster combines ARTEX with conventional automated tools to scan internet-facing systems, exploit flaws including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery, and install the open-source remote access tools WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2, which ARTEX agents download with netcat and curl (Microsoft, 2026-11-06). Microsoft's tell for an agent on a scanned system is "a wide variety of requests in a brief time", retries of variations on one technique and a move to next-stage actions at machine speed; ARTEX by default drives Nmap, curl, wget, Python HTTP clients and headless Chromium through Playwright, and blocking their default traits will not stop an agent, which "will quickly change them" (Microsoft, 2026-11-06). In Microsoft's testing, honeypots, decoys, tarpits and fake wins helped reduce the attack traffic reaching real assets, with no figures given (Microsoft, 2026-11-06).

Check Point Research counts 2,557 systems that host or hosted ARTEX panels, 1,608 of them live and public, and ten that exposed the full database; in those ten consoles the operators set a goal and then "barely interacted with their agent fleets" (Check Point, 2026-11-05). The campaigns it reads are opportunistic crime, not espionage: iOS signing certificates from grey-market shops, a cryptocurrency-service campaign and game-account credentials. In the signing-shop campaign the agents got in through hardcoded administrator passwords in JavaScript bundles, missing API authentication, command injection, insecure direct object references, weak administrative credentials and template injection (Check Point, 2026-11-05). Check Point does not name Storm-3358.

Open finding: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration →

item.title: Update: Cisco's mail gateway can be rooted by one crafted email; found in a TAC support case, exploitation confirmed
item.description: Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in root command execution: one merged on 2026-11-05 for the injection its author matches, at medium confidence, to the exploited CVE-2026-76461 and which needs URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service enabled, and one for the non-default S/MIME public-key harvesting feature that Rapid7 believes is CVE-2026-76443. A clean mail_logs check does not rule out the S/MIME injection, and Cisco's hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 build.
item.content:encoded:
Update07 Nov 2026 03:49 UTCrun 2026-11-07T0256Z-intelsummarycvesactionssourcesevidencesourcing_notebodytagsimmediate_action

Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in root command execution: one merged on 2026-11-05 for the injection its author matches, at medium confidence, to the exploited CVE-2026-76461 and which needs URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service enabled, and one for the non-default S/MIME public-key harvesting feature that Rapid7 believes is CVE-2026-76443. A clean mail_logs check does not rule out the S/MIME injection, and Cisco's hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 build.

Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public exploit modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in command execution as root. The first, merged on 2026-11-05, targets an injection in the Email Cloud Scanner URL-retrospective message database and its documentation says "URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service must both be enabled" (Rapid7 Metasploit module documentation, 2026-10-16), which sits against Cisco's statement that the flaw affects the gateway "regardless of device configuration" (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-09-14); its author says it can only be assessed with medium confidence that this is CVE-2026-76461, the flaw CISA lists, and that of the injections reproduced from the patch diff it was the only one that left the pattern COPY.*TO PROGRAM in mail_logs, the check Cisco's own advisory names (Rapid7 Metasploit pull request 22024, 2026-10-16). The second targets an injection in the S/MIME public-key harvesting feature, "we have reason to believe this maps to CVE-2026-76443" according to Rapid7's wrap-up of 2026-11-06 (Rapid7, 2026-11-06). The S/MIME module was merged on 2026-10-28; its author tested a gateway on AsyncOS 15.5.1-055 with the S/MIME Public Key Harvesting feature enabled for inbound mail, and the module sends one signed S/MIME email carrying 500 certificate addresses to the gateway's SMTP listener (Rapid7 Metasploit pull request 22018, 2026-10-15). Its documentation says "Public-key harvesting must be enabled on the inbound mail flow policy for the target to be exploitable" (Rapid7 Metasploit module documentation, 2026-10-15), and the author of the first module calls that feature "a different non-default feature" (Rapid7 Metasploit pull request 22024, 2026-10-16).

Cisco's hardening advisory lists CVE-2026-76443 with the other grouped CVEs and its fixed-release table gives 15.5.5-014 for 15.5 and earlier, 16.5.0-780 for 16.5 and "Migrate to a fixed release." for 16.0 (Cisco PSIRT, hardening-release advisory, 2026-09-14). A 16.0 appliance on 16.0.4-302 therefore has no named fix for the flaw the S/MIME module most likely uses; moving to 16.5.0-780 closes it. Rapid7 does not report exploitation of the S/MIME module's flaw, and Cisco does not say whether the injection it lists as exploited is the one in either module.

Open finding: CVE-2026-76461: Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated SQL injection in email parsing reaches root command execution, exploited before disclosure (CVSS 9.8) →

item.title: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
item.description: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, and Todyl's update of 2026-11-06 now assesses its operator as an automated agentic credential crawler, likely fed by secrets exposed in public repositories or web apps.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHupdatedNATOB2

Exposed application credentials: Microsoft sees an agentic framework search GitHub for OAuth and cloud application secrets and then sign in as the applications from 2026-10-28, and Todyl sees an operator use MSP applications to reach 27 organisations, government clients among them

Microsoft reports that since August 2026 threat actors have used the agentic offensive framework ARTEX to submit large volumes of queries to public GitHub for secrets (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05). As early as 2026-10-28 it saw successful service-principal sign-ins from two IP addresses, one a Tor exit node that may carry unrelated activity, across dozens of applications in several tenants, including a vendor-owned multitenant application whose credential was compromised at the source and used to reach multiple downstream tenants (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05). Microsoft states that a similar campaign involving the same addresses was also reported by Todyl (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Todyl, from its managed-detection telemetry, describes one operator who since 2026-11-01 has signed in to MSPs' Microsoft 365 and Azure environments as their own applications with stolen credentials that are still valid: about 45 app registrations at roughly 18 organisations were targeted, more than 33 authenticated, and 27 organisations were reached, among them the MSPs' downstream clients in government (Todyl, 2026-11-03). For nearly every credential the operator requests an Azure Resource Manager token, then a Key Vault token, and within minutes applications that had never been used start authenticating; MSP multitenant and delegated-admin apps and Partner Center tokens reach client tenants, one app sweeping 15 client tenants in about 10-second loops (Todyl, 2026-11-03). Todyl says no Microsoft vulnerability is involved and that it saw no persistence (Todyl, 2026-11-03). Its update of 2026-11-06 assesses the operator as an automated agentic credential crawler and the likely credential source as public repositories or web apps, citing credential scanning from the actor's address before the first sign-in, no sign of earlier compromise and custom-built affected apps (Todyl, 2026-11-03). After its detections fired on 2026-11-03 the operator switched to spoofed browser user agents and replayed users' refresh tokens, all blocked by Conditional Access (Todyl, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
Any Entra tenant, an MSP's or a customer's, that holds app registrations with client secrets, above all multitenant, delegated-admin and Partner Center applications and Azure DevOps service connections, security-tool integration apps among those abused (Todyl, 2026-11-03); Conditional Access for workload identities needs the Workload ID Premium licence and covers only single-tenant apps (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).
Detection
In Entra service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs, an invalid-secret or expired-secret error for an application followed by a success, one address authenticating as service principals in several unrelated tenants within 24 hours, an Azure Resource Manager token followed at once by a Key Vault token and then by previously unused apps authenticating, and failed service-principal sign-ins from hosting space that never succeed, which success-only logic misses (Todyl, 2026-11-03). In Azure DevOps auditing, personal access token creation and first use, federated service connections and pipeline edits (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Triage: the invalid-secret and expired-secret errors alone only show that someone holds an old or wrong credential for the app; Microsoft treats a failure followed by a success as the urgent case (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Defender takeaway
Inventory the client secrets on app registrations and hunt the sign-in pattern above in every tenant you run or manage, MSP-managed communal tenants included; on an affected app remove every client secret, certificate and federated credential, including those the actor added, and rotate what any Key Vault it could read holds, because tokens already issued stay valid until expiry (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Todyl updated its post on 2026-11-06 after Microsoft's research of 2026-11-05: it says Microsoft's findings match its assessment that the activity is an automated, agentic credential crawler, and it now names public repositories or web apps as the likely source of the stolen secrets, citing credential scanning from the actor's address before the first sign-in, no sign of earlier compromise and custom-built affected apps (Todyl, 2026-11-03). It quotes Microsoft for the GitHub access path and the ARTEX name, and adds that the operator replays harvested material within minutes, in one case signing in as a connector's app about 2.5 minutes after downloading its archive (Todyl, 2026-11-03).
